item.title: Is Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo worth $2,000? See how it stacks up against other foldable phones.
item.description: Preorders for the iPhone Duo began Friday, marking Apple’s debut in a foldable phone market largely dominated by Samsung and Google.
item.dc:creator: Genna Contino

item.title: ‘It’s a wait-and-see situation’: I’m 63 and diagnosed with lymphoma. Should I take my Social Security next year?
item.description: “My plan is to continue working as long as I’m able to do so and invest my Social Security benefits while I’m still earning a paycheck.”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: My wife says we can’t afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We’re in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?
item.description: “I worry about healthcare, long-term care, inflation, a long bear market and living to 95.”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: Can a $55,000-plus robot load the dishwasher? Inside my afternoon with two humanoid housekeepers.
item.description: Tau Robotics’ humanoids vacuumed my floors and wiped my counters — with some help from humans behind the scenes
item.dc:creator: Christine Ji

item.title: Nearly 40% of the S&P 500 is in a bear market. Here are 10 of those stocks that analysts say can gain up to 81%.
item.description: The S&P 500’s strong overall performance reflects its heavy weighting at the top. Under the surface, nearly 40% of the index’s stocks are down at least 20% from their 52-week highs.
item.dc:creator: Philip van Doorn

item.title: I’m 64 with two sons, but only one works in the family firm. Should I leave him 70% of the business?
item.description: “I have some reservations about the long-term stability of my younger son’s marriage.”

item.title: Here are the key things Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said — and didn’t say — while Americans were sleeping Thursday night
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh had the opportunity Thursday night to shape expectations before the central bank’s interest-rate-setting meeting in two weeks — and in keeping with his practice of leaving markets guessing, he chose not to.
item.dc:creator: Steve Goldstein
